chapter: Benny Carter, saxophones and Coleman Hawkins's last years
title: Metal and rubber mouthpieces
summary: Caldwell never had mouthpiece trouble; the section with Arthur Gibbs began using metal mouthpieces in 1927 and Hawkins did too.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

Well, you know, the people used— well, some people used rubber ones and Berg Larson and so forth. Well, Hawk changed his mouthpiece, didn't he?

Well, Hawk -- we were -- when the Berg Larson -- not the Berg Larson in -- it was the fellow, the first reed section we'd had up to Savoy with Arthur Gibbs. All of us started using the other metal mouth- piece (unintelligible) in New York later. And Hawk started to using them, and we all started to using them. But before that, though, Hawk was -- when I first heard him, Hawk played with a little metal mouthpiece then. It was rubber.
And then anything else changed, they were -- these mouthpieces came up before the Berg Larson got popular. This was back in 1927.
Oh, as early as that, was it?
Yeah. And we all started using these metal mouthpieces. But it never did prove too good for the altos.
No, it never did prove too good for the altos, and they used -- a few alto players used them, but finally went back to rubber mouthpieces.
